title: The Deliberation
corpus_scope: 17,848 ICLR 2026 panels (21a) · fourteen deliberations scored in full (21b) · 49,441 panels 2018–2026 (21c–d)
question: How does a panel's discussion usually end, and what does that ending correlate with?

figures.title: How deliberations usually go
figures.deck: Six panels in seven — 85.7% — never visibly move at all.

claims.statement: 85.7% of panels never show a judgment change.
claims.derivation: 15,289 panels with no recorded strengthen/weaken/reverse ÷ 17,848 rated panels × 100 = 85.66%, rounds to 85.7%

claims.statement: When judgments do move after the response, strengthening outnumbers softening and reversal combined, 3,543 units to 1,336.

figures.title: The repertoire: the five endings and their verdicts
figures.deck: The quiet endings accept least — silence 27%, entrenchment 54% (association, not cause) — and co-reviewers barely inspect the same things strangers would.

claims.statement: The quiet endings accept least — silence 27%, entrenchment 54%.
The overlap of inspected objects for reviewers of the same paper against reviewers of different papers: 0.27 versus 0.21.
claims.derivation: REP.overlap.real_hist (co-reviewers of one paper) vs. REP.overlap.base_hist (strangers), mean overlap of inspected objects

figures.title: The great quieting: 49,441 panels, year by year
figures.deck: Conversation bulges in 2022 and is squeezed shut by 2026 — silence falls 51% → 20%, then climbs all the way back to 52%.

claims.statement: Silence's share runs 51% → 20% → 52% from the first year, through 2022, to the last year.
claims.derivation: REP.by_year[y].silence for y = first year, 2022, and last year of the 49,441-panel 2018–2026 series

caveats.text: The five endings are machine-read from a field recording whether a reviewer's judgment strengthened, weakened, or reversed after the response; treat them as a census of what is visible in writing, not a verdict on any panel's diligence — a score changed without accompanying text never enters these counts.
caveats.scope: Fig 21a panel population and movement counts

caveats.text: Acceptance-rate differences between deliberation endings are an association, not a causal payoff of an ending: entrenchment accepts most partly because reinforcement includes reviewers reinforcing praise, and unanimity of silence often means unanimity about rejection.

The nine-year trend is descriptive only: the review format, submission volume, and reviewing culture all changed together over 2018–2026, and this figure cannot separate which of them drove the swing in silence.
